## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `af6dff1d84a58b6bf78e0d36661503717e8bb3aa`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/signed-body.ts, .changeset/34170-export-signed-body-readers.md + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/audit-seal-signed-body-readers-34170.integration.test.ts
Security-touching: yes

Read for this record: card #34170 with all 8 comments, PR #35895 (body, 4 files, net diff against `main`, merge base `8c18a362a2`), and the 58 check-runs on this head. Read but not reviewed, at this head: `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/package.json`, `src/audit-seal/index.ts`, `sealer.ts`, `amendment-writer.ts`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/audit-checkpoint.ts`, ADR-0154 (D11 and the residual-risk note), AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3.

Check-runs on this head: 58 runs, 38 `success`, 20 `skipped`, none failed or pending. `Check Changeset` ran twice (17:25Z and 17:58Z), both `success`. Build Core, TypeScript Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates), Test Core 10/10, Lint & Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard and the PR-body guards are `success`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **What the entry now adds: exactly four names. Right.** `src/index.ts` adds the values `checkpointBodyFromRow` and `amendmentBodyFromRow` and the types `CheckpointSignedBody` and `AmendmentSignedBody` to the existing ADR-0154 export block. Nothing else in the block moved. The two-dot diff against `main` shows no other plugin-audit file differs.
- **The `exports` map: only `.` is addressable. Right.** `package.json` has one entry, `.`, with `import` and `require` conditions, and `files` ships `dist` only. No subpath exists, so `./audit-seal/*` stays unreachable from outside, and the entry is the only door. The four names are the whole widening.
- **Nothing else became reachable. Right.** Still inside the package: `signedBodyBytes`, `checkpointDigest`, `checkpointRow`, `amendmentRow`, `checkpointLeafHashesFromRow`, `checkpointPartOf`, `chainKeyOf`, `SignedBodyError`, `canonicalJson` / `canonicalJsonBytes`, `AUDIT_CHECKPOINT_OBJECT`, `AUDIT_AMENDMENT_OBJECT`, the sealer and the signer.
- **Transitive types: unnamed from the entry, and that is sound.** `CheckpointSignedBody` refers to `AuditCheckpointKind` and `SealedColumnSet`. `AmendmentSignedBody` is the union of `RedactionAmendmentBody` and `ExpiryAmendmentBody`, which extend the module-private `AmendmentCommon`. None of the five is exported from the entry. The declaration bundle carries them as unexported declarations, which TypeScript accepts; Build Core and the consumer type gates are green on this head. A consumer reads every member and narrows the union on `kind`, but cannot name a union arm. That matches what the PR body calls the area ruling, option A. The ruling itself is not on the card thread (see ③).
- **One consequence the diff implies and nobody names:** the member shapes of those five types are now public by structure. Renaming or retyping a member of `RedactionAmendmentBody` is a change to the entry's surface, even though the name is not exported. No finding; it follows from option A.
- **`@public` TSDoc: consistent with the claim, uneven against the tree (N1).** Both readers carry `@public`, as the claim's file surface says ("on the two readers only"). The two exported types carry none, and no other entry export of this package carries the tag: these are its only two uses in plugin-audit. Nothing reads the tag: there is no API-extractor config, and the `api-surface` snapshot covers `packages/spec` only, so the dev's "no baseline exists for this package" is right.
- **No runtime behaviour changed. Right.** The `signed-body.ts` hunks are comment-only: no code line moved in either reader.

### ② Semver level

`patch` with `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.

- AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3: "The level follows the kind alone: a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves, `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`."
- `none` is the correct kind. `Metadata-protocol` is the change to what a metadata author can write. Two exported functions and two types add no key, value or metadata type.
- `Clause-②: yes` is the correct clause. The package's public surface widens. No arm is required ("at most one arm").
- Both declaration lines are line-initial in the changeset body and in the PR body, and they agree.
- `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head, twice. The claim's `minor` was the error, and the seat's level amendment (the latest card comment) corrects it. The changeset names one package, the one whose source moved.
- The changeset's title keeps `feat(...)`. Under the rule above the level follows the kind, not the commit type, and the gate agrees.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 7045478481 (blocked):
- Open question, how to commit after the refused `git commit`: closed by events. The re-claim 7045416162 records the maintainer's choice on the decision card, and report 7046786325 shows the commit made after it. It is a permission matter, not a contract one, and nothing in the tree depends on it.
- Out-of-scope note, the release comment says "never pushed" while origin held the branch at the base sha: accepted as stated. An empty marker push carries no work.
- Deviation, overlap-check after the commit: accepted. It has no effect on the contract.

Dev report 7046786325 (done):
- Open question, keep `patch`: **A, keep `patch`.** See ②.
- NOT MEASURED locally, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n`: answered by CI on this head (Build Core and Lint & Repo Gates are `success`).
- The note that `main` moved to `f44758b21e` after the local runs: answered by the check-runs, which ran on this head. The PR reads `mergeable_state: clean`.
- Deviations 1 to 5 (overlap-check order, push before verification, trailers, attribution lines, worktree removal): process only, the lane seat's to accept. None touches the exported surface.
- `security_findings: none`: I agree that the diff opens no hole (④). The record still reads `Security-touching: yes`, because the changed hunks export readers of the tamper-evidence mechanism and teach what a signature covers.

Escalated to the seat:
- **E1, the tier.** The committed tree touches no published schema and no governed path, so by the template's own rule the face is the declaration one, which maps to `TIER_DEFAULT`. The release comment 7044194641 says the same ("a `TIER_DEFAULT` L2 is owed"). This record is served at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` because the claim cites a seat ruling asking for it. The seat should confirm that the record reader accepts a record served above the face's tier before it posts.
- **E2, two rulings I could not read.** The seat ruling of 05:26Z (shape, `@public`, tier) and the area ruling "option A" (two return types only) are quoted in the claim, the release comment and the PR body, but neither is a comment on the card. I judged both points on the tree, and both hold on their merits.
- **E3, the PR is still a draft.**

SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no production query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. The only reads are the test's two `engine.find` calls on one-row tables.

### ④ Design judgment

**Against the card's acceptance scenario: holds.** The sealer hands the sink the object it signed (`sealer.ts`, `signBody` then `deliver`), and stores `checkpointRow(body, ...)`, which itself passes the body through `checkpointBodyFromRow`. The amendment writer does the same with `amendmentRow`. So the stored row is the reader's own normal form plus the unsigned columns, and reading it back gives the delivered members. The live verifier reads stored rows through the same two functions, so a sink's re-read and the verifier's read cannot drift apart. That is the property the card asks for. The pin proves it on a real kernel for a `window` checkpoint and a redaction amendment, with the readers imported through `../index.js`.

**Against ADR-0154: holds.** D2: a body carries commitments, roots, digests and handle ids, never a value, salt or seed, so exporting the body types publishes nothing that `AuditCheckpointSinkEntry.body` did not already describe member by member in `packages/spec`. D11: the sink seam is unchanged; the export serves the contract's own sentence, "it can re-read the stored records".

**Attempts to break it:**
- *Forge or build a signed body.* Not possible through the new surface. The readers are pure: a row in, a validated body out. No signer, no key, no engine. `checkpointRow`, `amendmentRow` and the signer stay internal. A caller able to write `sys_audit_checkpoint` rows could do so before this PR.
- *Weaken verification.* No. `verifier.ts` and `bundle.ts` are untouched, and the readers are the functions the verifier already trusts.
- *A body that verifies for a row it should not.* I found none. The signature covers `sealed_object`, `tenant_id` and `sequence`, so a body cannot be moved to another chain or position. The reader ignores `id`, `chain_key`, `leaf_hashes` and, on an amendment, the other kind's columns. Changing those leaves the signed bytes unchanged, which is correct: they are not signed. Driver spellings (`"7"` for a count, `1` for a flag, a `Date` for an instant) fold to one body by design. An absent `tenant_id` is refused, never read as the deployment chain. `previous_digest` absent on a sequence above 0 is refused.
- *Hidden state.* One coupling: the reader refuses any `canon_version` other than the installed `AUDIT_SEAL_CANON_VERSION` (N3).
- *Stability as a contract.* Output members are fixed by the spec's sink contract and by the signature itself, so they cannot move without breaking stored signatures. Pre-amendment checkpoints (no `part_index`, `final_part`) read back without the two keys, so their bytes stand.

**Findings:**

S1 (should-fix) — The public TSDoc and the changeset say the reader "answers the body the sink was handed". That holds only for a row nobody changed. The reader checks shape, never authenticity, and a missed checkpoint waiting for re-delivery is exactly the row a host operator can still rewrite (ADR-0154: "Whoever holds the database and either key can re-sign"). The readers' own neighbour says it for its case (`checkpointLeafHashesFromRow`: "and its signature checked"); the two `@public` readers do not. Add one sentence to each TSDoc and to the changeset: the reader validates and normalizes, it does not verify the signature, and a rewritten row yields a body that fails verification (or, re-signed by a key holder, one that only the off-host trust anchor catches). Not blocking: the export weakens nothing, and the residual risk is the ADR's own, stated there.

S2 (should-fix) — The acceptance speaks of the entry and its signed bytes; the export gives the body only. A sink outside the package must assemble the entry itself (`kind` from the table, `keyId` from `body.signing_key_id`, `signature` from the row's `signature` column) and bring its own RFC 8785 serializer, because `signedBodyBytes` and `canonicalJson` stay internal. The pin shows this: its reader comes through the entry, but its bytes and its key check come from `./signed-body.js`, `./jcs.js` and `./signer.js` by path. The contract still holds, since first delivery leaves the sink in the same position and the pin asserts `row.signature` and `signing_key_id` against the delivered entry. Fix in this PR by stating the assembly in the TSDoc or changeset, and carry to cloud#4128 whether `signedBodyBytes` should follow, so the consumer does not copy the serialization the card set out not to copy.

N1 (nit) — `@public` sits on the two readers only: not on the two exported types, and on no other entry export of the package. Nothing reads the tag.

N2 (nit) — `SignedBodyError` is not exported, so the changeset makes the error's `name` string the contract. That is workable and it is stated. `AUDIT_CHECKPOINT_OBJECT` and `AUDIT_AMENDMENT_OBJECT` are likewise internal, so the changeset's two literal table names are what a sink queries by.

N3 (nit) — The reader accepts only the installed `AUDIT_SEAL_CANON_VERSION` (1). Now that it is public, a later canonical form must keep version 1 rows readable, or a sink cannot backfill older checkpoints. Worth a line where the constant is next bumped.

N4 (nit) — The pin compares with `toEqual` and JCS bytes, so member order is not pinned. It need not be: the contract is the RFC 8785 form. Today's order happens to match the sealer's.

No must-fix.

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d6a679c374e6e29a7765d6f81fca7276ae80261e`

Check-runs on this head: 57 runs, 39 `success`, 18 `skipped`, none failed or pending. Build Core, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Lint & Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard, the PR-body guards and `Check Changeset` (twice) are `success`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The round is comment and changeset prose only. Confirmed on the tree.** The commit touches two files: `signed-body.ts` (+30 / −4) and the changeset (+5 / −1). Every changed `.ts` line is a TSDoc line: the count of changed non-comment lines is 0. `src/index.ts`, the test file and `package.json` are unchanged from `af6dff1d84`.
- **The public surface is what it was.** The entry still exports the same four names; `signedBodyBytes` stays internal, as the dev reports. Every ① judgment of record 7046919186 stands.

Unchanged: `patch`, `Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Both declaration lines are still line-initial in the changeset. `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head. The judgment of record 7046919186 stands.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 7047779338:
- `open_questions`: none.
- Deviation 1, the dev wrote the PR body in a patch round: process only, the seat's to accept; the coordinator's order named it.
- Deviation 2, the worktree was recreated and removed: no effect on the contract.
- NOT MEASURED locally (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n`, `check:type-check-debt`): answered by CI on this head, where Build Core, Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are `success`.
- `security_findings: none`: not agreed for this round. See M1.

Still open from record 7046919186, for the seat: E1 (the committed tree maps to the declaration face, so confirm the reader accepts this above-tier record), E2 (the two quoted rulings are not on the card) and E3 (the PR is still a draft).

SQL push-down: no finding. No query was added.

### ④ Design judgment

Each new sentence, against the code:

- "read from an unaltered stored row, it answers the body the sink was handed": right.
- "It validates and normalizes; it never verifies the signature": right. Neither reader takes a key or reads `signature`.
- "A rewritten row reads back into a body that fails verification": right for a signed column. Two cases are left out (N5).
- "or, re-signed by whoever holds the signing key, into one that only the off-host trust anchor catches": **wrong. See M1.**
- "So a sink verifies the row's `signature` over the rebuilt body, under a key it trusts itself, before it treats the row as delivered": sound as an instruction. It catches a changed signed column and a key the sink does not trust.
- The entry assembly: right. `kind` is `'checkpoint'` or `'amendment'`, as `AuditCheckpointSinkEntry.kind` declares. `keyId` is `body.signing_key_id`: the sealer and the amendment writer never store a signature whose key id differs from the one in the bytes. `signature` is the row's `signature` column, which `checkpointRow` and `amendmentRow` write.
- "this package does not export one": right. Neither `signedBodyBytes` nor `canonicalJson` is in the entry.

**Findings:**

M1 (must-fix) — The sentence says a row re-signed by the signing-key holder is caught by "the off-host trust anchor". In this tree a trust anchor is the party that vouches for a public key (`IAuditCheckpointSigner.trustedPublicKey`: "This is the trust anchor `os audit verify`'s live check reads"; `verifier.ts`: "A signature is `ok` only under a key the trust anchor vouches for"). A row rewritten and re-signed with the genuine signing key verifies under exactly that key, so the trust anchor does not catch it, and neither does the check the next sentence prescribes. What catches it is the copies already off the host: a later checkpoint's signed `previous_digest` no longer matches the rewritten one (ADR-0154: such a holder "can rewrite rows, recompute roots and re-sign the chain", and only "taking checkpoints off the host as they are signed" closes that). The trust anchor catches the other case, a row signed under a key planted on the host. The sentence appears three times: both reader TSDocs and the changeset, which ships as `CHANGELOG.md` and is not amendable in place after release. It teaches a sink author that a signature check under a trusted key covers a key-holder rewrite, on the one path, re-delivery, where the row has no off-host copy yet.

The wording came from this reviewer's own S1 in record 7046919186, which was loose in the same way; the dev took it faithfully. The fault is the record's first, and it is corrected here.

A fix that matches the code, in all three places: "A rewritten row reads back into a body that fails verification. A row rewritten and re-signed under a key planted on the host fails under a key the sink trusts itself. A row rewritten and re-signed by whoever holds the genuine signing key verifies; only the copies already off the host catch it, because a later checkpoint's signed `previous_digest` no longer matches. So a sink verifies ..." The last sentence can stay as it is.

N5 (nit) — "A rewritten row reads back into a body that fails verification" leaves out two cases: a rewrite of an unsigned column (`id`, `chain_key`, `leaf_hashes`) reads back into the same body, and a malformed rewrite is refused with `SignedBodyError`. The M1 rewrite can take "a row whose signed columns were rewritten" in passing.

Closures against record 7046919186:
- S1: not closed. The three points asked for are present (unaltered row, no signature check, the sink verifies under its own trusted key), but the added clause is wrong. It is reopened as M1.
- S2: closed. The assembly is stated in both TSDocs and the changeset, and the PR body carries the `signedBodyBytes` question as a Carry line.
